profile.headline: Platform Engineer | Internal Tools, Developer Platforms & Self-Service Systems | Turning Complex Workflows Into Scalable Infrastructure
profile.summary:
Hi, I’m Paul! I’ve never been particularly good at leaving things the way I found them.

At twelve, that meant building a RuneScape fan site, which turned into running private servers. Later it was modding my Wii, changing code in RPG Maker, messing with Minecraft plugins, and building websites.

Professionally, I took a different route.

I worked my way from cashier to running retail stores, then moved into e-commerce managing 10,000+ products, and later digital marketing. I spent years on the other side of the systems I now build—managing data, launching content, running experiments, and working around tools designed by someone else.

Eventually, those two paths met.

I joined Hims & Hers as a Web Content Specialist and progressed through CMS Developer to Software Engineer. Today, I build platforms: internal tools, self-service systems, data infrastructure, and developer tooling that turn complicated, engineering-dependent workflows into capabilities other teams can safely operate themselves.

The systems vary, but I keep finding myself drawn to the same problem:

Something important depends on a person knowing, remembering, or manually doing too much.

That’s usually where I get interested.

Sometimes the answer is automation. Sometimes it’s validation, documentation, a better abstraction, or giving someone the right information at the right moment. And sometimes the right answer is not to build a platform at all and just ship the thing.

My background means I’ve spent a meaningful part of my career on both sides of the tools I now build. I think that’s made me a different kind of engineer: I care as much about whether a system makes someone’s work better as I do about how it’s built.The technology has changed a lot since that first RuneScape website.

The motivation really hasn’t.

I still want to know what’s happening behind it.

And then I want to see if I can make it better.

profile.about:
Hi, I’m Paul! I’ve never been particularly good at leaving things the way I found them.

At twelve, that meant building a RuneScape fan site, which turned into running private servers. Later it was modding my Wii, changing code in RPG Maker, messing with Minecraft plugins, and building websites.

Professionally, I took a different route.

I worked my way from cashier to running retail stores, then moved into e-commerce managing 10,000+ products, and later digital marketing. I spent years on the other side of the systems I now build—managing data, launching content, running experiments, and working around tools designed by someone else.

Eventually, those two paths met.

I joined Hims & Hers as a Web Content Specialist and progressed through CMS Developer to Software Engineer. Today, I build platforms: internal tools, self-service systems, data infrastructure, and developer tooling that turn complicated, engineering-dependent workflows into capabilities other teams can safely operate themselves.

The systems vary, but I keep finding myself drawn to the same problem:

Something important depends on a person knowing, remembering, or manually doing too much.

That’s usually where I get interested.

Sometimes the answer is automation. Sometimes it’s validation, documentation, a better abstraction, or giving someone the right information at the right moment. And sometimes the right answer is not to build a platform at all and just ship the thing.

My background means I’ve spent a meaningful part of my career on both sides of the tools I now build. I think that’s made me a different kind of engineer: I care as much about whether a system makes someone’s work better as I do about how it’s built.The technology has changed a lot since that first RuneScape website.

The motivation really hasn’t.

I still want to know what’s happening behind it.

And then I want to see if I can make it better.
